He was impressed by the 'tenacity' of AI agents, observing them persistently solve problems humans would have abandoned, describing it as a moment of feeling 'AGI'. LLMs dramatically increase stamina, a key bottleneck in development.

LLM coding will likely divide engineers into those who 'love coding' and those who 'love building'. Builders are enthusiastic about AI coding, while those who value code craftsmanship are less comfortable – a trend already visible.
The productivity gap between 10x engineers may widen with AI, as the ability to effectively utilize AI tools becomes a significant differentiator in performance.
He predicts 2026 will be the year of the 'slopacolypse', warning that AI-generated low-quality content will flood all digital media – GitHub, Substack, arXiv, and social networks.
IDEs remain essential, not just for terminal-based coding, but for reviewing and accepting/rejecting AI-suggested changes via diffs.
GPT-5 models represent a significant leap forward compared to GPT-4, particularly in complex tool calling within agent loops.
evidenceEn: Many commenters echoed the concern about 'complacency' being a bigger issue than atrophy. Accepting AI’s code suggestions without critical evaluation can lead to disinterest in the project. LLMs gravitate towards their training data, making experimentation difficult.
Some countered the claim of AI 'tenacity', citing instances of Sonnet models making extensive, unnecessary code modifications or even giving up, while Opus showed fewer such issues.

A retired developer used Claude for two weeks on an Intel 8096 firmware reverse engineering project and was able to create disassemblers, assemblers, and emulators, raising concerns for small utility vendors.

One commenter drew parallels to the DevOps movement, noting that achieving 10x performance with AI requires changes to workflows, design, and team culture – similar hurdles that hindered widespread DevOps adoption.

A skeptical response stated that after a year of hearing 'AI is changing everything,' there’s no evidence of 10x improvements in quality or output, suggesting that unsubstantiated AI coding anecdotes should be banned on Hacker News.
howToApplyEn: To mitigate AI agents pushing code in unwanted directions, explicitly define design principles and coding conventions in files like CLAUDE.md or project rules and configure the AI to reference them in each session. Place core rules at the system prompt level to prevent the AI from 'forgetting' initial instructions as context grows.

To prevent Sonnet from getting stuck in debugging loops, use the Opus model for complex debugging and insert checkpoint prompts like 'are you on track?' Alternatively, set up a hook to automatically halt execution if the number of changed files exceeds three.
To boost productivity with AI while preventing skill degradation, divide roles: write core algorithms and architecture yourself, and delegate boilerplate, test code, and repetitive tasks to the AI.
Reports indicate significant improvements in GPT-5’s tool calling performance. If building complex multi-tool agent loops, test switching from GPT-4 to GPT-5 (reasoning=minimal).

title: SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning

ko.oneLiner: LLM 에이전트의 스킬 라이브러리는 RL 학습 중 경험에서 재사용 가능한 스킬을 자동 추출하고 에이전트 정책과 함께 진화하여 기존 메모리 기반 방법 대비 15.3% 이상 성능을 향상시킨다.
keyFindings: 성공한 trajectory뿐 아니라 실패한 trajectory도 수집해서 각각 '성공 패턴'과 '실패 교훈(failure lesson)'으로 변환 — 기존 방법들이 실패를 버리던 것과 반대
스킬을 General Skills(탐색 전략 등 범용)과 Task-Specific Skills(태스크별 세부 절차)로 나눈 계층형 라이브러리 SKILLBANK 구성, 추론 시 임베딩 유사도로 검색
raw trajectory 저장 대비 스킬 추출로 10~20배 토큰 압축 달성 — 컨텍스트를 덜 써도 더 좋은 성능
RL 학습 중 validation 실패를 분석해 새 스킬을 추가하거나 기존 스킬을 개선하는 재귀적 진화 메커니즘 — 스킬 라이브러리가 정적 DB가 아니라 살아있는 지식 베이스
Cold-start SFT(지도 파인튜닝) 단계로 베이스 모델이 스킬 활용법을 먼저 학습한 뒤 RL 진입 — 없으면 성능 20% 하락
Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 기반으로 GPT-4o를 ALFWorld에서 41.9%p, Gemini-2.5-Pro를 29.6%p 앞지름
howToApply: 에이전트 롤아웃 시 성공/실패 trajectory를 모두 저장하고, GPT-4o·o3 같은 teacher 모델에게 성공 패턴과 실패 원인을 JSON 스킬 형태로 추출하게 한다. 스킬 포맷은 'id, 제목(3~5단어), 원칙(1~2문장), 적용 조건'으로 구성.
추출한 스킬을 General(모든 태스크 공통)과 Task-Specific(태스크 유형별)로 분리해 SKILLBANK를 만들고, 추론 시 General은 항상 포함, Task-Specific은 임베딩 코사인 유사도 Top-K로 검색해 컨텍스트에 주입한다.
RL 학습 중 일정 주기(예: 5 step마다) validation을 돌리고, 성공률이 임계값(δ=0.4) 미만인 태스크 카테고리의 실패 trajectory를 모아 teacher 모델에게 분석시켜 신규 스킬 1~3개를 SKILLBANK에 추가한다.

en.oneLinerEn: An LLM agent's skill library automatically extracts reusable skills from experiences during RL training, evolving alongside the agent's policy to improve performance by over 15.3% compared to traditional memory-based methods.
en.targetAudienceEn: ML engineers experiencing limitations with prompt-based agents like ReAct and Reflexion, and considering RL-based agent training. Specifically, researchers or developers who want to enable agents to accumulate past failures as reusable knowledge.
keyFindingsEn: Collects both successful and failed trajectories, converting them into 'success patterns' and 'failure lessons' – contrasting with existing methods that discard failures.

Constructs a hierarchical skill library, SKILLBANK, categorizing skills into General Skills (e.g., exploration strategies) and Task-Specific Skills (detailed procedures for each task), and retrieves them via embedding similarity during inference.
Achieves 10-20x token compression by extracting skills instead of storing raw trajectories – achieving better performance with less context.

Implements a recursive evolution mechanism that analyzes validation failures during RL training to add new skills or improve existing ones – making the skill library a living knowledge base, not a static database.
Utilizes a cold-start SFT (Supervised Fine-Tuning) stage where the base model first learns how to utilize skills before entering RL – resulting in a 20% performance drop without it.
Outperforms GPT-4o by 41.9%p and Gemini-2.5-Pro by 29.6%p in ALFWorld using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as the base model.
evidenceEn: ALFWorld success rate of 89.9% – a +12.3%p improvement over the base GRPO (77.6%) and a +27.4%p improvement over the strongest memory-augmented RL (SimpleMem+GRPO 62.5%).
WebShop success rate of 72.7% – a +6.6%p improvement over the best comparison (GRPO 66.1%).
Average of 47.1% across 7 Search-augmented QA tasks – a +4%p improvement over EvolveR (43.1%) and a +19.4%p improvement over EvolveR on a single task in Bamboogle.
Average prompt length reduced by 10.3% to approximately 1,300 tokens compared to raw trajectory memory (approximately 1,450 tokens), while achieving higher performance.
howToApplyEn: Save both success and failure trajectories during agent rollouts, and have a teacher model like GPT-4o or o3 extract success patterns and failure causes into JSON skill format. The skill format should consist of 'id, title (3-5 words), principle (1-2 sentences), application conditions'.

Separate the extracted skills into General (common to all tasks) and Task-Specific (by task type) to create SKILLBANK. Always include General skills during inference, and inject the top-K most similar Task-Specific skills based on embedding cosine similarity.

During RL training, run validation periodically (e.g., every 5 steps), and if the success rate for a task category falls below a threshold (δ=0.4), collect the failure trajectories and have the teacher model analyze them to add 1-3 new skills to SKILLBANK.
